chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to me from his uncle, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi, from Ibn Fadhal, from al-Mithami, from Abi Basir, who said:

I entered upon Umm Hamidah to console her regarding Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). She wept, and I wept because of her weeping. Then she said: 'O Abu Muhammad, if you had seen Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at the time of death, you would have seen something amazing.' He opened his eyes and said: 'Gather for me everyone who is a relative between me and him.' She said: 'So we did not leave anyone out; we gathered them all.' He said: 'Then he looked at them and said: Indeed, our intercession will not reach one who considers Salat unimportant.'
ai.seo_question: Who will not receive the intercession of the Imams according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) final words, where he gathers his relatives to emphasize that the Ahl al-Bayt’s intercession is not a blanket guarantee but contingent upon the preservation of Salah. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that neglecting prayer constitutes a form of *istikfaf* (trivialization) that severs the bond of spiritual eligibility for intercession, linking personal piety directly to eschatological hope.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Ali Majluwayh from his uncle from Muhammad b. Ali al-Qurashi from Ibn Fadhal from al-Maythami from Abi Basir who said:
“One who considers Salaat unimportant will not receive our intercession.”
